newsitem.title: USA: Port Richey, Fla., rejects merger with neighbor.
newsitem.headline: Port Richey, Fla., rejects merger with neighbor.

text.p: Voters in Port Richey, Fla., soundly defeated a proposal to merge with the neighboring city of New Port Richey, elections officials said.
The merger was rejected 673-216, a margin of 3-1, in Tuesday's election.
Port Richey city leaders held the election in hopes of staving off a legislative attempt to dissolve Port Richey and annex it to its larger neighbor.
The bill calls for a September referendum allowing residents in both cities to vote.

One of the bill's sponsors, Sen. Jack Latvala, R-Palm Harbor, said he drafted it after receiving complaints from Port Richey rsidents alleging political infighting and ethical wrongdoing. He said he would review Tuesday's election results before pressing forward.
The central Gulf Coast cities are in Pasco County. Port Richey has about 3,000 residents and New Port Richey about 12,000, according to the Florida Almanac.
